name: crawled_multi_next_swing
provenance: REAL crawled board — character 'Nodding', snapshot 76, captured 2026-08-04T17:18:39.000Z (patch 2026-08-04, report 94), crawl path 'strength'. Generated by tools/audit/build_nonpaladin_fixtures.py (3d D1). WHY THIS BOARD: MULTIPLE ON-NEXT-SWING ABILITIES, DUAL-WIELDING — added `3o` Block D to close `AUDIT_3N` F5. `3n` Block B is the arc's biggest modelling fix (next-swing abilities ride the swing clock and REPLACE the swing they ride), and it shipped with two behaviours no fixture could test, because EVERY committed fixture holds exactly ONE next-swing ability: `build_elric_paladin` has Lightbound Cleave alone and `build_crawled_cp_melee` has Heroic Strike alone. The auditor ran both natural mutants — deleting the shared-budget decrement (so two Cleaves ride ONE white swing) and making leg 2 reduce the OFF hand as well — and BOTH STAYED GREEN across the whole harness. This board carries TWO next-swing abilities on TWO weapons — Stormbound Cleave (907364) and Heroic Strike (25286) — which is what makes those two mutants visible: budget SHARING needs >=2 competitors, and main-hand-ONLY replacement needs an off hand to leave alone. Exercises: joint consumption bounded by one swing budget, highest-damage-first allocation order, and `auto_oh` untouched by replacement. ⚠ WHY THIS BOARD AND NOT A THREE-ABILITY ONE: the first candidate carried THREE next-swing Cleaves, which is a stronger sharing test — but all three resolve to the SAME 283 damage per swing, so the ORDERING arm could not discriminate any order from any other and would have passed vacuously on a tie. Here the two differ genuinely (Stormbound 268/swing against Heroic Strike 121/swing), so allocating in the wrong order gives the budget to the weaker ability and the arm fires. `AUDIT_3N` F5 asked for two abilities of DISTINCT per-swing damage and the distinctness is the whole point. 🛑 Chosen on MECHANICS (two ids carrying Attributes & 0x4 on one dual-wield board), never on the character's name — and it is a real cohort member the gate already sims through this code. 🛑 STATS ARE GEAR-ONLY. They come from character_snapshots.gear_stats_json, which carries an explicit _gearOnly key — no path grant, no talent, no buff, no base stats. That is why the primary stats look far too low for level 60. THIS FIXTURE IS NOT A DPS PREDICTION AND ITS ABSOLUTE OUTPUT MEANS NOTHING; it exists to exercise engine code paths a single-paladin harness cannot reach. Weapon damage IS real — parsed from the item description and self-checked against that description's own stated DPS.

ground_truth_absent._detail: This fixture is a CRAWLED board, not a capture. Its stat block, gear and cards come from the site's armory snapshot; there is no combat log for it and no per-hit magnitude anywhere. The character's crawled encounter DPS exists in encounter_performance, but using it here would not be an independent check - it is the SAME number the calibration gate already scores this character against, so the fixture would assert what the gate asserts and add nothing.
ground_truth_absent._what_would_close_it: A combat log from a character running this kind of board, paired with a same-session AscensionCrafterExport - i.e. the Mage capture's protocol applied to a combo-point melee (or a DoT caster). The owner is the only source. Until then a target here would be invented, and an invented target is worse than none because it looks like evidence.
ground_truth_absent._do_not: Do NOT back-fill this from the sim's own output, from the crawl's aggregate DPS, or by analogy with the Mage. 3e correctly declined to back-fill the six ContentProfile presets by analogy; this is the same rule.
